CRANIAL MRI AND CRANIAL MR ANGIOGRAPHY

Technique: Sagittal and axial T1-weighted; sagittal, axial, and coronal FLAIR; axial T2-weighted, DWI, ADC, and SWI. Vascular-weighted in the transverse plane in the arterial direction towards the circle of Willis with 3D TOF technique, with reconstructions in sagittal and coronal planes using MIP technique.

Comparison: [date_1] dated cranial MRI

Findings:

A lesion is observed in the central region of the pons, hypointense on T1-weighted sequence, hyperintense on T2-weighted sequence, and hypointense on SWI sequence. No contrast-enhanced examination was performed. It is stable over an 18-year interval and was primarily evaluated as capillary telangiectasia.

Bilateral basal ganglia, thalamus, midbrain, medulla oblongata, and cerebellum are normal.

Pituitary gland and pineal gland are normal.

Cavum septum pellucidum is observed.

Acute infarct was not detected on diffusion and ADC sequences.

The width of the third and lateral ventricles and hemispheric sulci is normal.

In the cranial TOF MR angiography examination:

The contours, caliber, and flow signal intensity of the petrous, cavernous, and supraclinoid segments of the bilateral internal carotid arteries are normal.

The contours, caliber, and flow signal intensity of the A1 and A2 segments of both anterior cerebral arteries are normal.

The contours, caliber, and flow signal intensity of the M1 and M2 segments of both middle cerebral arteries are normal; trifurcation segments are normal.

Distal segments of both vertebral arteries are normal. The basilar artery is in the midline, and its contours, caliber, and flow signal intensity are normal.

The contours, caliber, and flow signal intensity of the P1 and P2 segments of the bilateral posterior cerebral arteries and the superior cerebellar artery are normal.

No aneurysm or vascular pathology was observed in the arterial structures forming the circle of Willis.

Cranial bone structures, both globes, retrobulbar fat tissue, optic nerves, and optic chiasm are normal.

Impression:

•	A lesion observed in the central region of the pons, hypointense on T1-weighted sequence, hyperintense on T2-weighted sequence, and hypointense on SWI sequence, stable over an 18-year interval, primarily evaluated as capillary telangiectasia
•	Cranial MR angiography findings within normal limits.

In sections passing through the supratentorial region, the 3rd and lateral ventricles are midline and of normal width.

There is T2-FLAIR hyperintense signal increase present in the periventricular white matter secondary to chronic ischemic changes.

Central and peripheral CSF spaces show atrophic dilatation.

Variation of the cavum septum pellucidum et vergae was observed.

Multiple T2-FLAIR hyperintense gliotic foci located in the bilateral centrum semiovale corona radiata, bilateral frontotemporoparietal subcortical and periventricular white matter, reaching up to 5 mm in diameter, are observed (Fazekas grade 3).

Within the prepontine cistern, a well-defined extra-axial, lobulated contour, multiseptate cystic lesion is observed. It measures 38 mm in craniocaudal length, 33 mm in anteroposterior diameter, 56 mm in transverse diameter. It is T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense, showing wall contrast enhancement after IV contrast agent. It appears hyperintense on diffusion-weighted images (epidermoid cyst? Main cerebral vascular structures are patent.

Cranium bony structures, both globes, retrobulbar fat tissue, optic nerves, and optic chiasm are normal.

Within the included sections; paranasal sinuses and mastoid cell aerations are intact.

Impression:

•	Atrophic dilatation of central and peripheral CSF spaces.

BRAIN (CRANIAL) MRI
Clinical information: Headache. Encephalomalacia in the left caudate nucleus.
Technique: 3-plane T1-weighted, FLAIR; axial T2-weighted, SWI, and DWI.
Findings:
Brainstem and cerebellum, 4th ventricle, and posterior fossa cisterns are normal.
There is a chronic cystic infarct measuring 19 x 13 x 10 mm, cone-shaped (sagittal 144), with its base on the ependymal surface and apex extending inferolaterally, in the superior posterior portion of the head and anterior portion of the body of the left caudate nucleus, involving the superior portion of the anterior limb of the internal capsule, and gliosis around it. No evidence of chronic hematoma is observed on SWI sections.
Other basal ganglia, thalami, and internal capsules are normal. The corpus callosum is slightly thickened but there is no obvious dysplasia.
The second notable finding is the absence of the septum pellucidum. The frontal horns of the normal-sized lateral ventricles are pointed anteriorly and inferiorly and are "box-shaped". The fornices, lacking septal support, have collapsed inferiorly.
Both ACA A1 segments are present, but there is a single A2 (azygous ACA). The azygous ACA bifurcates at the genu of the corpus callosum. This finding is suggestive of congenital absence of the septum.
Absence of the septum can accompany many cerebral malformations. However, no other pathology related to cerebral or optic pathways or the hypothalamo-hypophyseal axis has been detected in the patient.
Other sections of cerebral white and gray matter and cerebral sulci are normal.
Paranasal sinuses and middle ear aeration, nasopharynx, and orbits are normal.
Impression:
•	Chronic cystic infarct in the left caudate nucleus head-body and anterior limb of the internal capsule.

•	Congenital absence of the septum pellucidum and azygous anterior cerebral artery anomaly.

•	No cerebral, optic, or hypothalamic-hypophyseal pathology/malformation accompanying the congenital anomaly has been detected.

* Tuberculum sellae meningioma extending into the sella, most likely infiltrating the optic chiasm, with atrophy and gliosis in the left optic nerve.

In the herniated lobe, a necrotic cavity with irregular contours 3.5 cm in diameter, local dural thickening, and a focal epidural non-infectious collection developed at the upper limit of the necrosis.

• Lesion involving the posterior wall of the left frontal sinus, orbital roof, and lateral wall, causing massive hemorrhage and edema in the left frontal lobe, resulting in mass effect and subfalcine shift.

o The enhancement pattern rules out metastasis or infection.

• Increasing leukoencephalopathic changes in the brainstem and cerebral white matter.
